question:
Let $f: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function defined by $f(x) = e^{x^2}$. Define a relation $R$ on $\mathbb{R}$ by $aRb \iff f(a) = f(b)$.

(a) Show that $R$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathbb{R}$.

(b) Find the equivalence classes of $R$.

(c) If $g(x) = e^x + e^{-x}$, find all $x$ such that $f(x) = g(x)$.

(d) Considering your answers in (b) and (c), discuss whether there exists a one-to-one correspondence between the set of equivalence classes of $R$ and the set of real solutions to $f(x) = g(x)$.

options.A:
(a) $R$ is not an equivalence relation because it is not symmetric
(b) $[a]=\{a\}$ for every $a$
(c) $f(x)=g(x)$ has infinitely many real solutions
(d) A one-to-one correspondence always exists
options.B:
(a) $R$ is an equivalence relation on $\mathbb R$
(b) $[a]=\{a,-a\}$ for $a\ne0$ and $[0]=\{0\}$
(c) According to the given solution, $f(x)=g(x)$ has no real solution
(d) Hence there is no one-to-one correspondence between the equivalence classes and the set of real solutions
options.C:
(a) $R$ is reflexive but not transitive
(b) $[a]=\mathbb R$ for all $a$
(c) $f(x)=g(x)$ has solution $x=0$ only
(d) There is exactly one equivalence class
options.D:
(a) $R$ is symmetric but not reflexive
(b) $[a]=\{a+1,a-1\}$
(c) $f(x)=g(x)$ has solutions $x=1,-1$
(d) There is a one-to-one correspondence with two classes
